findings.science: Partial reflection into air and reflection-angle law retained. Fixed incident intensity and ordinary unpolarized scope prevent the single-polarization Brewster counterexample. For the ordinary air-to-water/glass dielectric interface the unpolarized reflectance has the stated overall strengthening trend and tends to 1 as incidence tends to 90 degrees. Air-to-higher-index transmission still exists below that limit; this is not TIR. See independent reasoning in sci-outcome.json.
findings.language: Both versions say toward 90 degrees, nearly parallel and almost all, not exact normal-to-grazing finite equality or a TIR claim.
